발표 준비에 필요한 작업 조건: Task requirements for preparing a presentation
“내일 발표인데, 오늘 시작했습니다.” 에이전트에게 일을 맡기는 상황은: “My presentation is tomorrow, and I only started today.” A task delegated to an agent might begin this way. Asking for “slides and a script for a five-minute presentation” may produce a draft quickly. But work remains after the slides exist: checking the supporting sources, trimming the material to fit the time, and understanding anything the presenter cannot explain. After stepping away, the presenter must also know what has been checked and what needs revision. The following hypothetical presentation scenario illustrates these requirements.
The expected deliverables are a slide file, a script, and sources for the main claims. Completion is checked by opening the file, reading the script within five minutes, and verifying that the sources support the claims. The agent drafts and revises the material; the presenter reviews the final content and submits it. Defining the outcome and permitted scope first makes it possible to choose the necessary capabilities.
발표를 준비하는 동안 모델은 다음에 조사할 내용이나 수정할 문장을 판단한: During preparation, the model decides what to research next or which sentences to revise. Search tools retrieve material, and document tools create files. The harness connects the model and tools, manages conversations and execution results, and provides the execution environment for continuing work. <v0/> explains the basic concept. A harness for this task must actually support the flow from searching to reviewing.
하네스를 고를 때는 세션, 메모리, 도구 연결, 권한 제어, 멀티에이전트: When choosing a harness, consider sessions, memory, tool connections, permission controls, multiple agents, and operation. After reading that a feature exists, ask what it must do for your task. Can you revise the presentation requirements, inspect the completed file, and restrict unauthorized sending?
하네스 생태계에서 사용자가 구성하는 범위: How much of the harness do users configure?
하네스 생태계는 사용자가 어느 부분까지 직접 구성하는지를 기준으로 이해할: One way to understand the harness ecosystem is by how much users configure themselves. They may configure existing software with conversation, session management, and tool-use capabilities, or developers may implement the work stages and state management in code. This is a perspective for making a choice, not a division of products into two mutually exclusive categories. Intermediate approaches include adding tools to existing software or implementing only part of a workflow.
OpenClaw와 Hermes Agent는 세션, 도구와 작업 실행을 관: OpenClaw and Hermes Agent are examples of software that manages sessions, tools, and task execution. Users connect models and tools and configure the working environment. Later, we compare their specific capabilities using the same presentation task.<v0/> LangGraph is a tool for constructing the workflow itself: a framework and runtime that defines state and execution stages as a graph, continues execution, and provides points for human intervention. It is best understood as a component for building such a program’s execution flow, rather than a finished application that immediately produces slides. <v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-20; no version specified in the web documentation).
발표가 내일이라면 새로운 실행 환경을 만드는 데 쓸 수 있는 시간이 짧다: If the presentation is tomorrow, little time is available to build a new execution environment. There is good reason to first check whether familiar tools support research, file creation, and review. If the same slide format is needed every week and multiple people must review it, investing time in repeatable research and approval procedures may make sense. Consider troubleshooting and maintenance as well as initial setup time.
따라서 생태계를 살펴보는 첫 질문은 자신이 직접 구성할 필요가 있는 부분: The first question is therefore which parts you need to configure yourself. Distinguishing built-in capabilities, features available through configuration, and functions requiring additional tools helps narrow the candidates. The scope users must manage also affects the six selection criteria below.
중단한 작업을 이어가는 세션과 메모리: Sessions and memory for resuming interrupted work
자료를 조사하다 잠시 자리를 비운 뒤 돌아왔다. “어디까지 했더라?”라는: Suppose you return after a break from researching. Answering “Where was I?” requires finding the previous conversation and tool executions. A session is a unit that groups the conversation and execution records within a workflow. Reopening it lets you continue using previous requests and results. However, the entire stored history is not necessarily supplied to the model unchanged on every turn. The Hermes Agent session documentation distinguishes stored conversation history from the context the model receives for each response. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-20).
작업을 이어갈 때는 대화 기록과 함께 현재 상태를 확인해야 한다. 검색한: Resuming work requires checking the current state as well as the conversation. To choose the next action, you need to know which of ten sources were retained, which claims still lack verified sources, and which file is the latest draft. A short working document can record this information. “Two official sources checked; permission-control explanation needs further checking; slides are at draft two,” for example, tells you where to begin next.
한편 “분명 5분 발표라고 했는데, 왜 30장이지?”라는 문제는 작업 조: “I said five minutes, so why are there 30 slides?” raises a different question: whether task requirements persist. Distinguish conditions applying only to this task from information reused across tasks. “This presentation is five minutes long” is a task-specific condition. “Write explanations in simple Korean” may be a lasting preference if it applies to future work. Memory can be understood as a mechanism that stores and supplies information for use across sessions.
시간이 5분에서 3분으로 바뀌었다면 현재 작업 문서의 조건을 수정하고,: If the time changes from five minutes to three, update the requirement in the working document and apply it to the existing script. Recording an earlier requirement does not establish that the current deliverable is correct. Alongside storage capabilities, check whether you can inspect, correct, and delete information stored incorrectly.
세션을 이어가는 방법과 새 세션에서 작업 문서를 읽는 방법은 모두 검토할: Both resuming a session and reading a working document in a new session are options. Resume the existing session when detailed discussion is still needed; if the goal and materials are organized, select the information the new task needs. <v0/> covers the detailed design of memory and task state.
결과물을 만드는 도구와 실행 권한: Tools for producing deliverables and permission to execute
“PPT를 만들었다는 말 말고, 파일을 주세요.” 발표 준비에서 도구 연: “Please give me the file, not just a statement that you made a PPT.” This request illustrates why presentation work needs connected tools. Users must be able to receive, open, and edit the file. That requires tools to search and read sources, software to generate slides, and a way to inspect the result visually. Check the required file format and application when choosing a setup. Even when a file can be created, open it to verify that text and charts display correctly in the presenter’s environment.
도구를 연결하는 방식 중 하나가 MCP(Model Context Prot: MCP, the Model Context Protocol, is one way to connect tools. It is a protocol for exchanging information and making calls between AI applications and external capabilities. It provides a structure for discovering and using available functions, but it does not define a particular slide-generation capability or the quality of the finished product. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-20; documentation version: 2026-07-28).
스킬(skill)은 도구를 언제, 어떤 절차로 사용할지 안내하는 지침을: A skill packages instructions about when and how to use tools. It might direct the agent to inspect every slide after generating a deck and fix clipped text. OpenClaw defines skills as instruction files explaining how and when to use tools. Adding a skill still requires checking that the necessary software and permissions are available. <v0/> covers tool, MCP, and skill connections in detail. <v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-20).
파일이 완성되자 에이전트가 교수에게 보내겠다고 한다면 “전송은 잠깐만요”: If the agent offers to send the completed file to the professor, a “Wait before sending” condition is needed. In this example, reading sources and drafting are permitted, while the presenter submits the work personally. Actual tool and environment permissions must match these instructions. Permission control determines the capabilities available, resources accessible, and actions requiring human confirmation.
여기서 도구 선택과 실행 범위의 제한을 구분해야 한다. 예를 들어 파일: Tool selection and restrictions on execution scope are distinct. Disabling a file-writing tool does not create a read-only environment if a command tool can still modify files. OpenClaw’s official documentation likewise explains that allowing or blocking tool names does not restrict every side effect within a command. A sandbox limits the execution space and access scope and must be checked alongside tool policies. Define the sources, output folders, and external connections needed for the presentation, and check whether the final submission channel is accessible to the agent. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-20).
역할 분담과 지속 실행의 조건: Dividing roles and keeping work running
발표 준비가 늦어지면 조사와 검수를 나누어 맡기고 싶어진다. 멀티에이전트: When preparation falls behind, it may be tempting to split research and review. A multi-agent setup divides roles among agents and combines their results. One agent could organize the sources used in the presentation, while another compares their claims against the originals. Review must wait until the claims and sources are ready. Ordering dependent tasks is part of dividing roles.
“한 명은 조사, 한 명은 출처 확인”이라는 역할 이름만으로는 충분한 작: Role labels such as “one researches, one checks sources” rarely provide sufficient instructions. Give the reviewer the topic, sentences to check, source list, and required output format. Ask it to record which claims match which evidence and what needs revision. Assigning responsibility for editing the final slides also reduces simultaneous changes to the same file.
이때 하위 에이전트가 이전 대화를 얼마나 전달받는지에 따라 작업을 맡기는: Delegation depends on how much earlier conversation the subagent receives. OpenClaw offers both a fresh context and a fork of the parent conversation. Hermes Agent’s default delegation tool starts a new conversation and uses the goal and context supplied by the parent as task information. Project instruction files may still be included separately in Hermes, so a new conversation does not mean an environment with no instructions or context. <v0/>, <v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-20).
역할을 나누면 에이전트별 호출과 결과를 합치는 과정도 추가된다. 적은 분: Dividing roles adds calls for each agent and work to combine the results. For a short deck, one agent performing research and review sequentially may be easier to manage. Decide whether to use several agents based on whether the work can be divided, whether handoff information is ready, and whether the additional calls and review are affordable. Multiple agents do not, by themselves, make their errors independent or source verification accurate.
밤이 되면 다른 질문이 생긴다. “나는 자도 작업은 끝나야 하는데, 계속: At night, another question arises: “Can I leave it working while I sleep?” Continuing a task already underway differs from scheduling a new task for a specified time. If the execution environment is off at the scheduled time, the task cannot run then. OpenClaw’s scheduled jobs run in its Gateway process, and Hermes agent schedules likewise require the Gateway to be running. Here, Gateway means the resident program managing requests and execution. <v0/>, <v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-20).
발표 준비를 밤새 맡기려면 완료 조건과 중단 조건을 함께 정한다. 가령: Before leaving presentation work running overnight, define stopping conditions as well as completion criteria. For example, have the agent save its review results, but stop and record items whose sources are inaccessible or require additional approval. Check where runtime, retries, and usage can be limited in the actual configuration. Items without built-in limits may need separate operational controls. The next day, the records should show whether the work succeeded and what remains.
같은 발표 과제로 OpenClaw와 Hermes 비교하기: Comparing OpenClaw and Hermes on the same presentation task
이제 두 하네스를 같은 과제에 적용해 볼 수 있다. 조건은 5분 분량의: We can now apply both harnesses to the same task: creating five minutes of slides and a script, checking sources for the main claims, and leaving final submission to the presenter. The comparison below applies officially documented configurations to this task. It does not report measured speed or quality from producing slides with either product.
먼저 발표용 작업 기록을 어떻게 찾고 이어갈지 비교한다. OpenClaw: First, compare how presentation records are found and resumed. OpenClaw can organize sessions by the conversation’s entry channel and user. However, direct messages share the main session by default, so separating users or channels requires configuring session scope. Hermes can find and resume saved sessions by name or identifier. For this example, consider checking OpenClaw’s conversation routes and session scope or naming and reopening a presentation session in Hermes. Assess whether each product’s procedures for separating and retrieving work records fit your usage. <v0/>, <v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-20).
메모리는 저장할 정보의 종류와 불러오는 방법을 대조한다. 확인한 문서에서: For memory, compare the kinds of information stored and how they are loaded. In the documentation examined, OpenClaw distinguishes <v0/> for user preferences, <v1/> for lasting facts, and daily work logs. An API is an interface through which other programs use a service’s functions. The application obtains information about available tools, and the agent selects those needed for the request. name: presentation-draft
description: Use when dividing a presentation manuscript into slide titles, key points, and speaker notes suited to the audience and presentation time.
---

Inputs are the user’s manuscript, audience, and presentation time.
If the audience or time is missing, ask before drafting.

1. Find one sentence in the manuscript expressing the conclusion the audience should retain.
2. Divide the material needed to understand that conclusion into slides and determine their order.
3. Write the on-screen title and key points for each slide.
4. Put explanations that will not fit on screen and transitions to the next slide in the speaker notes.

Return a Markdown draft for each slide in this order: title / key points / speaker notes.

It examines what each preserves and what it leaves out.</v0>
§7.1에서 설명했듯이 하네스(harness)는 언어 모델을 감싸서 파일: As §7.1 explains, a harness surrounds a language model, manages conversation history and tools such as file reading and command execution, and continues work through a loop of input, decision, execution, and feedback. Context is less of a concern when a task ends after a few iterations. But implementing several features or investigating a persistent bug may require dozens or hundreds of iterations, accumulating more history than the model can see at once. Users also often stop and return the next day. Here, a session means a unit of work in which a tool is opened and one conversation continues. How the harness reduces, reloads, and restores context can determine whether that work succeeds.
이 절의 도구 기능 설명은 각 도구의 공식 문서를 기준으로 한다. 기능은: Tool capabilities in this section are described using their official documentation. Because features change frequently, each source includes the date and version checked.

What an agent appears to “remember” is context: input the harness sends back to the model with each request. As an analogy, context is the collection of materials spread across the model’s desk; each response uses only what is on that desk at the time. A coding agent’s context roughly includes the following.
하네스가 정한 시스템 지침과 도구 목록: System instructions and the tool list defined by the harness

MCP tools and skills are additional capabilities, such as external-service connections and task procedures (§7.3).
컨텍스트에는 상한이 있다. 이 상한을 컨텍스트 윈도(context win: Context has a ceiling called the context window, corresponding to the desk’s size in the analogy. Its size is measured in tokens, the units a model uses to process text, which can be thought of as fragments somewhat smaller than words (see tokens and context windows in the glossary, and §5.2). During long tasks, tool results often fill context faster than conversation. Reading a log with hundreds of lines or an entire file can add the equivalent of dozens of exchanges at once.

Replacing it with a summary is called context compaction. Because the harness determines this behavior, the same model may retain different information in different harnesses.
Using Claude Code as an example, compaction can be described in the following stages. Other tools follow a broadly similar flow but differ in detail.

3. 체크포인트와 Git의 역할: 3. The roles of checkpoints and Git
이어 가기와 별개로, 에이전트가 잘못된 방향으로 파일을 고쳤을 때 되돌리: Apart from continuing work, agents need a way to undo file changes that head in the wrong direction. Two mechanisms serve this purpose: checkpoints for quickly returning to a recent state, and Git commits for retaining a lasting record. Like a save point in a game, a checkpoint remembers files at a particular moment. Git manages file-change history, and a commit stores the changes at that point with an explanation.
Major tools offer the following checkpoint features.
대화 턴을 시작하는 요청을 보낼 때마다 자동 저장: Automatically before every request starting a conversation turn

<v0/>. 파일과 대화를 되돌리고 원래 도구 호출을 다시 제안: <v0/>. Restores files and conversation and proposes the original tool call again

이전 요청의 Restore Checkpoint. 이후 요청은 대화에서 제: Restore Checkpoint on an earlier request; later requests are removed from the conversation
Claude Code의 되돌리기 메뉴에는 “여기부터 요약” 같은 선택지도: Claude Code’s rewind menu also includes options such as “Summarize from here.” This reduces context by summarizing part of the conversation without changing files, connecting checkpoints with the compaction discussed in section 1. <v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-20)
<v0>복원 범위의 한계.</v0> 체크포인트는 에이전트의 편집 도구가: <v0>Limits of restoration.</v0> Checkpoints primarily track files changed by the agent’s editing tools. Claude Code documentation states that they do not track changes made solely through Bash commands, meaning commands executed directly in the terminal rather than through editing tools, or changes from other sessions or external sources. Checkpoints do not replace version control. Their data is cleaned up after roughly 30 days by default. <v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-20; Claude Code 2.1.329) VS Code documentation likewise states that executed terminal commands, network requests, deployments, and external-service changes are not undone. <v2/> (accessed: 2026-11-20) Cursor describes checkpoints as local storage separate from Git, intended only for undoing agent changes. <v3/> (accessed: 2026-11-20)
예를 들어 에이전트가 데이터베이스에 테스트 데이터를 넣거나 파일을 외부: For example, if an agent inserts test data into a database or uploads files to external storage, restoring code from a checkpoint does not remove those effects. It is safer to configure permissions so these actions require human approval before execution (§7.2, §8.3).
따라서 두 장치는 다음처럼 나누어 쓴다. <v0>체크포인트로 빠르게 되돌: Use the two mechanisms for different purposes: <v0>restore quickly with checkpoints, and preserve accepted results with Git commits.</v0> Checkpoints let you move back a few steps after a failed attempt; commits preserve changes that pass tests and should remain. The new-session procedure in section 2 ends with a commit because commit history persists across sessions and tools.
중간발표의 토론 질문은 “긴 작업은 이전 대화를 재개할까, 새 세션에 인: The midterm discussion asked, “For a long task, should we resume the previous conversation or hand off to a new session?” The following criteria synthesize this section. They are the author’s recommendations, not measured comparisons across tasks.
짧게 중단했고 같은 작업을 이어 간다: A short interruption, continuing the same task
결정과 경과를 다시 설명하지 않아도 된다: No need to restate earlier decisions and progress
세션에서 압축이 여러 번 일어났다: The session has undergone several compactions
이전 내용이 이미 요약으로만 남아 있다: Earlier content already survives only as a summary
작업 방향이나 목표가 바뀌었다: The direction or goal has changed
이전 시도의 기록이 새 작업의 판단을 흐릴 수 있다: Previous attempts may distort decisions about the new task
에이전트가 같은 실수를 반복한다: The agent repeats the same mistake
실패한 방법을 인수인계 노트에 적어 다시 시도하지 않게 한다: Record failed approaches in the handoff note to prevent another attempt
어느 방법을 쓰든 공통 조건이 있다. 지켜야 할 규칙은 지침 파일에, 진: Both methods share the same requirements: keep lasting rules in instruction files, task state in progress files, and accepted changes in Git commits. These records provide a basis for continuing whether compaction, resumption, or a new session occurs.

개인 연구에서 AI와 함께 문서 검색 에이전트를 만들었다. 질문을 받으면: In my own research, I built a document-search agent with AI. Given a question, it finds and reads documents and answers using their contents. To reserve room for composing the answer, the final stage allowed only reading documents already found or ending the response. After five preparatory tests passed, I ran the actual questions. Yet one execution log showed another search during the final stage. The code contained a condition checking tool use. How had the search passed that check?

모델은 코드를 어떻게 이어 쓰는가: How does a model continue writing code?
대규모 언어 모델(LLM)은 텍스트를 토큰(token)이라는 단위로 처리: A large language model (LLM) processes text in units called tokens. It divides text into pieces, assigns each a fixed numerical identifier, and uses those identifiers in computation. Grouping common character combinations into one token lets the same text be processed in fewer units than character-by-character processing. One word may be a token or span several tokens. In code, tokens may also be parts of variable names or punctuation such as parentheses. Boundaries depend on the model’s tokenization method.
텍스트를 생성할 때 모델에 전달된 요청과 지금까지 생성한 텍스트가 컨텍스: During text generation, the request supplied to the model and the text generated so far form part of its context: information used to predict the next token. The model computes probabilities for possible tokens at the next position, appends the selected token, and uses the newly extended text on the next step. Using previously generated tokens to predict subsequent ones is called autoregressive generation. <v0>Tom B. Brown et al., Language Models are Few-Shot Learners</v0> (arXiv v4, 2020-07-22, §2.1).
그림 2: 자연어 문장에 다음 토큰을 붙이는 과정. 토큰을 나누는 방식과: Figure 2: Appending the next token to a natural-language sentence. Token boundaries and candidate probabilities are illustrative.
코드를 작성할 때도 같은 방식으로 다음 토큰을 이어 붙인다. 예를 들어: Code is generated by appending tokens in the same way. Suppose the task is “Run the requested tool if it is on the allowlist.” In Python, a conditional begins with <v0/>, and <v1/> tests whether a value belongs to a collection. If the code already defines a variable holding the requested tool, the model can reuse that name in the condition, then generate the line that executes when the tool is listed. It outputs one token at a time. The context for each position may include the request and variable names defined several lines earlier.
그림 3: 다음 토큰을 선택하고 출력에 붙이는 한 차례. 코드 조각과 후: Figure 3: One step of selecting and appending a token. Code fragments and candidate probabilities are illustrative.
모델은 많은 코드에서 앞부분을 보고 다음 토큰을 예측하는 학습을 반복한다: Models repeatedly learn to predict the next token from prefixes of many code examples. They learn relationships such as where an earlier variable name is reused and which code follows a conditional inside a loop. For a new request, those learned relationships inform the probabilities of tokens continuing the current context. In the 2026 Mellum 2 study, pretraining used roughly 10.6 trillion tokens of code, natural language, and other material; code-related data made up 59% of the final training stage. The pretrained Mellum 2 base model scored 62.4% by <v0/> on MBPP, an evaluation requiring short Python programs from natural-language descriptions. <v1>Marko Kojic et al., Mellum2 Technical Report</v1> (arXiv v1, 2026-05-29, §3.1, §3.2, Table 5). <v2>JetBrains, Mellum2-12B-A2.5B-Base-Pretrain model card</v2>. <v3>Jacob Austin et al., Program Synthesis with Large Language Models</v3> (arXiv v1, 2021-08-16, §2.1, §3).
“결제가 끝난 주문의 금액을 합산해 줘”라는 요청을 받았다고 하자. 주문: Suppose the request is “Sum the amounts of paid orders.” After writing code that iterates over orders, the model may assign higher probability to code that checks payment status and adds the qualifying amounts. Repeating these predictions completes multiple lines one token at a time.
그럼에도 예상치 못하게 틀리는 이유: Why they still fail in unexpected ways
모델은 익숙한 패턴을 바탕으로 코드를 작성할 수 있다. 문법에 맞고 자연: Models can generate code using familiar patterns. Even syntactically valid, readable code can produce incorrect results by omitting a necessary condition or mishandling particular inputs. The 2026 PROBE study evaluated code from six models and found incorrect answers caused by oversimplifying problem conditions or failing to consider some inputs. <v0>Rodrigo Pato Nogueira et al., PROBE: Benchmarking code generation in large language models</v0> (2026-08-15, §5.4.4).
코드가 테스트를 통과해도 실제 실행에서는 틀린 결과를 낼 수 있다. 테스: Code can also pass tests yet fail in actual use. A test can catch an error only if its input makes the faulty code produce a different result. One HumanEval+ problem required listing numbers common to two lists in ascending order. AI-generated code passed the original tests, but for a new input the correct answer was <v0/> and the actual output was <v1/>. Converting the sorted numbers into a set (<v2/>) at the end changed their order. <v3>Jiawei Liu et al., Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation</v3> (arXiv v3, 2023-10-30, Figure 1).
앞의 주문 합산 예시에서 할인이 없으면 상품 가격을 그대로 더한다. 할인: In the order-total example, an undiscounted order contributes its full price, while a discounted order should contribute the price minus the discount. Suppose the model instead adds the discount. Testing only an undiscounted 10,000-won order never executes the faulty discount branch. A 2,000-won discount exposes the error: the expected amount is 8,000 won, but the code calculates 12,000 won.

마무리 단계에서 검색이 실행된 이유: Why the search ran during the final stage
도입부에서 검색이 실행된 이유도 프로그램이 도구 사용을 허용할 때 잘못된: The search in the introduction also ran because the permission check referenced the wrong list. The program had both a complete registry of tools and an allowlist for the current stage. During the final stage, only document reading and ending the answer were allowed. When the model requested a search, the program checked the complete registry. Search was registered there, so the program executed it. The preparatory tests had not exposed this incorrect list reference.

마무리 단계에서 검색이 차단되는지 테스트하면, 전체 목록을 검사하는 코드: A test checking that final-stage searches are blocked fails when the code consults the complete registry and passes when it consults the current allowlist.

AI의 코드 작성 능력이 발전하면서 프로그래밍을 전공하지 않은 사람도 만: As AI code generation improves, people without programming backgrounds can more easily start vibe coding by describing a desired function and using AI-generated code. Once the code runs, check whether it actually respects the intended conditions. In this example, that means sending a search request during the final stage and checking that execution is blocked.
9장 「AI 코딩은 어떻게 실패하는가」에서는 그럴듯하지만 틀린 코드와 요: Chapter 9, “How AI Coding Fails,” examines failures such as plausible but incorrect code and edits outside the requested scope. Chapter 10, “Verifying That It Works,” begins in §10.1 with turning requirements into tests, then discusses reproducing errors and tracing their causes through execution records.

블루베리는 산성 토양을 좋아한다. 이걸 모르고 비싸고 좋은 화분용 배양토: Blueberries like acidic soil. What happens if you do not know this and carefully repot one in expensive, high-quality potting mix? It dies. That is how my blueberry plant died.
코딩도 농사와 비슷하다. 흙의 산도가 블루베리의 생육을 좌우하듯, 사소해: Coding resembles growing plants. Just as soil acidity determines whether blueberries thrive, an entire system sometimes depends on one seemingly trivial line. Perhaps only Mr. Kim, the manager who left in 2006, knows why it remains in an otherwise functioning program. Suppose you ask a coding tool, “Clean up this code, but preserve all current functionality.” To answer, it must infer why Mr. Kim’s line is there and respect the user’s constraint while refactoring.
8.1절에서 본 것처럼 언어 모델이 하는 일은 앞의 텍스트를 보고 다음: As Section 8.1 explains, language models predict the next token from preceding text. They have therefore been criticized as “stochastic parrots” that probabilistically concatenate linguistic forms found in training data without understanding their meaning (<v0>Bender et al., On the Dangers of Stochastic Parrots: Can Language Models Be Too Big?</v0> (FAccT 2021 main conference)). How, then, can next-token prediction produce an answer reflecting code context and user requirements? This section does not decide whether models “understand” context. It examines how training makes their outputs reflect it.
코딩 모델을 만드는 과정은 크게 <v0>사전학습</v0>과 <v1>사후학: Building a coding model can be broadly divided into <v0>pretraining</v0> and <v1>post-training</v1>. Pretraining aims to produce a <v2>base model</v2> with capabilities useful across tasks such as writing, completing, and understanding code. It may start from an already trained model and broaden that foundation. Post-training aims to improve abilities and behaviors more directly relevant to actual use. Someone requesting code cares whether the conditions are respected and the submitted code behaves as intended. Both stages can improve correctness. They differ in the model developers aim to build at that stage and the evidence used to judge improvement (<v3>Llama 3 technical report, §3–4</v3>).
사전학습: 여러 작업에 쓸 코딩 능력을 어떻게 기르는가: Pretraining: developing coding capabilities for many tasks
프로그램 하나에는 개발자가 내린 수많은 결정이 기록되어 있다. 어떤 이름: A program records countless developer decisions: naming choices, functions called together, and implementations of agreements stated in comments. Pretraining learns these relationships from large amounts of code and documentation. Once a base model exists, researchers can evaluate its ability to complete unfamiliar functions or propose implementations from descriptions. Code Llama researchers started from Llama 2, which had already learned language, continued training on code, and then built instruction-following models on that expanded coding foundation. Continuing from an existing model also occurs during pretraining (<v0/>).
그렇다면 개발자가 남긴 파일만 있고 별도의 답안지가 없을 때는 무엇을 기: What provides a learning target when only developers’ files exist, with no separate answer key? The answer is <v0>next-token prediction</v0>, introduced in Section 8.1 as a generation method. During training, the same prediction becomes the objective. Because the training program has the original text, it can compare the probability assigned to each next token with the token actually present. Assigning low probability to that token produces a larger error. Training gradually adjusts <v1>weights</v1>, the internal numerical values affecting predictions, to reduce this error. Repeating the comparison across many positions removes the need for humans to label every line. Obtaining training targets from the data itself is called <v2>self-supervised learning</v2>. Here, the target is the original token. Even a token in buggy code remains the training target (<v3>Radford et al., Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training, §3.1, Equation (1)</v3>).
어떤 문맥을 보여 줄지도 정해야 한다. 함수가 정의된 파일과 호출되는 파: The context shown during training must also be chosen. Reading a function’s definition and its callers together supplies its uses as well as its name and implementation. Training can also simulate editing with code already following the cursor. <v0>Fill-in-the-middle</v0> removes a middle segment and asks the model to reconstruct it from surrounding code. Grouping files determines the context available; fill-in-the-middle determines the problem posed within it. This provides the first answer to the introduction’s question: models learn to reflect code context by seeing contextual material together and predicting within it (<v1/>; <v2>Bavarian et al., Efficient Training of Language Models to Fill in the Middle</v2>).
사전학습과 사후학습의 경계가 늘 뚜렷한 것은 아니다. Cheng 등은 문: The boundary between pretraining and post-training is not always sharp. Cheng and colleagues generated requests and matching responses from documents and used those question-answer pairs alongside the originals as pretraining data. This introduced the response format during pretraining. The distinction between the stages thus depends on the training objective rather than solely on the data format (<v0>Cheng et al., Instruction Pre-Training: Language Models are Supervised Multitask Learners</v0> (EMNLP 2024 main conference)).
사후학습: 사용자에게 어떤 답을 하도록 가르치는가: Post-training: teaching the model what kind of answer to give
기본 모델이 코드를 쓸 수 있어도 사용자가 바란 답을 매번 내놓지는 않는: A base model may write code without consistently giving the user the desired answer. It may rewrite the whole file when asked to show only the changes, or produce a plausible result while omitting a constraint. Post-training defines desirable responses and further trains the model in that direction. The targets include actual problem-solving capability as well as response format.
이렇게 이미 학습한 모델의 가중치를 목적에 맞게 더 조정하는 것을 <v0: Further adjusting an already trained model’s weights for a purpose is called <v0>fine-tuning</v0>. What information guides those adjustments during post-training? We examine supervised fine-tuning from example responses, preference learning from comparisons, and reinforcement learning that rewards the model’s own attempts. Real training pipelines may combine these methods (<v1/>; <v2/> (published in Nature)).
모범 응답을 보여 줄 수 있는가?: Can we show the model an example response?
<v0>지도 미세조정(SFT)</v0>에서는 사용자 요청과 그에 맞는 모: <v0>Supervised fine-tuning (SFT)</v0> trains on pairs of user requests and example responses. The model reads the request and response prefix and predicts the response’s next token. This uses the same next-token prediction as pretraining. The important difference is that developers have selected <v1>the answer they want the model to give for this request</v1>. During Llama 3 instruction fine-tuning, the researchers excluded request tokens from loss computation and adjusted weights using the response the model should generate (<v2/>).
모범 답은 누가 쓸까? 사람이 직접 작성할 수도 있고, 다른 모델이 완성: Who writes the example answer? A person may write it, or another model may generate it. Using a teacher model’s responses as training targets for a student is <v0>response-based distillation</v0>. In Kim and Rush’s experiment, the teacher translated a full source sentence, and the student learned from that translation. DeepSeek-R1 later used teacher-generated solutions to fine-tune smaller language models. Here, distillation describes <v1>whose answers are learned</v1>, while supervised fine-tuning describes <v2>how the student is trained on those answers</v2> (<v3>Kim and Rush, Sequence-Level Knowledge Distillation, §3.2</v3> (EMNLP 2016 main conference); <v4>DeepSeek-R1, distillation experiments</v4>).
응답을 이용한 증류는 업계에서 다투는 문제이기도 하다. 모델을 만든 회사: Response-based distillation is also contested within the industry. One party may collect another company’s model responses at scale for training without its permission. OpenAI’s November 2026 GPT-6.2 system card described extraction of hidden chain-of-thought as a primary distillation attack against frontier laboratories. Countermeasures included training models not to reveal hidden reasoning, classifiers detecting extraction attempts, and protection for encrypted reasoning. In the company’s own adversarial evaluation, average success for attacks extracting earlier-turn reasoning fell from 54.0% for GPT-6 Astra to 0.2% for GPT-6.2 Astra (<v0/> (official company document; published: 2026-11-17; accessed: 2026-11-22)). These are company-reported figures without external verification. Nevertheless, they show that obtaining example answers for SFT is not solely a technical issue.
두 응답 중 나은 것을 고를 수 있는가?: Can we choose the better of two responses?
좋은 답을 새로 작성하기는 어려워도 이미 나온 두 답을 비교하기는 쉬울: Comparing two existing answers may be easier than writing a good one from scratch. <v0>Preference learning</v0> can use a request, a chosen answer, and a rejected answer as one training example. A representative method, <v1>direct preference optimization (DPO)</v1>, uses these comparisons to adjust weights so that the chosen answer becomes more probable relative to the other answer than it was under a reference model. Evaluators need only identify their preferred answer, without assigning separate numerical scores (<v2>Rafailov et al., Direct Preference Optimization, §4</v2> (NeurIPS 2023 main conference)).
코딩에서는 실행 결과가 선택의 근거가 되기도 한다. Qwen2.5-Cod: In coding, execution results can guide preference. After supervised fine-tuning, the Qwen2.5-Coder researchers used tests to check correctness on independently executable algorithmic problems and language-model judgments for more complex code. They constructed preference data from these evaluations and applied DPO. Tests determined which code was preferred; the response-generating model learned from the resulting <v0>comparisons</v0> (<v1>Qwen2.5-Coder technical report, §4.2</v1>).
모델이 직접 만든 답에 보상을 줄 수 있는가?: Can we reward the model’s own answers?
<v0>강화학습(RL)</v0>에서는 훈련 중인 모델이 답을 시도하면 평: In <v0>reinforcement learning (RL)</v0>, the model attempts an answer and receives an evaluation as a <v1>reward</v1>. The learning algorithm uses rewards from multiple attempts to adjust the model toward answers expected to earn higher rewards. For programming problems, submitted code can run against specified tests, with the results contributing to the reward. DeepSeek-R1 researchers used such feedback for tasks with verifiable answers, including competitive programming. Comparing this with DPO clarifies the two uses of the same code tests: one determines a preference between responses, while the other rewards a response attempted by the model. The principle also applies when responses contain tool calls for file reading or command execution. Section 8.3 explains their actual execution, and Section 8.4 explains why tests can provide fast, reliable criteria (<v2>DeepSeek-R1, reward design</v2>; <v3/>).
프로그램으로 정답을 검사하기 어려우면 사람의 판단에서 보상을 얻기도 한다: When programmatic answer checking is difficult, rewards can come from human judgments. InstructGPT researchers trained a <v0>reward model</v0> using human rankings of multiple responses. That model scores new answers humans have not yet evaluated. Its scores then guide reinforcement learning of the response-generating model. This is one way human preferences enter actual model training (<v1>Ouyang et al., Training language models to follow instructions with human feedback, Figure 2</v1> (NeurIPS 2022 main conference)).
The methods discussed so far can be summarized as follows.
원본 코드에서 실제로 이어진 토큰: The tokens that actually follow in the original code
정의와 사용 위치, 앞뒤 코드 같은 맥락: Context such as definitions and uses, and surrounding code
요청에 맞는 모범 응답: Example responses suited to the request
두 응답 가운데 더 나은 쪽: Which of two responses is better
테스트나 사람의 판단으로 매긴 보상: Rewards based on tests or human judgments
이런 방법들로 학습시킨 모델도 여전히 다음 토큰을 예측한다. 달라지는 것: Models trained this way still predict the next token. What changes is what those predictions reflect. Pretraining predicts contextual material together, allowing surrounding code’s purpose, such as Mr. Kim’s line, to influence token probabilities. Post-training rates answers respecting the requested conditions more highly, allowing user constraints to influence them too. This answers the introduction’s question: regardless of whether models “understand” context, they can be trained to produce outputs reflecting it.
다만 어떤 조건이 반영될지는 사람이 정한 평가 기준에 달려 있다. 무엇을: Which conditions are reflected depends on human-defined evaluation criteria. Conditions absent from the choice of example responses, preferred answers, or rewards are difficult to learn. Just as care alone cannot save a blueberry plant when its grower does not know soil acidity matters, effort does not compensate for missing criteria.
지금까지 본 방법은 모두 자료와 피드백으로 가중치를 조금씩 조정하는 훈련: All methods discussed so far gradually adjust weights using data and feedback. In November 2026, Takehi and colleagues at MIT CSAIL described a different approach in a blog post. They gave GPT-6 Astra the weights of Qwen3.5-0.8B and a Python environment for inspecting them. The small model repeatedly looped during reasoning instead of answering, hitting its output limit on 93.0% of evaluation questions. Astra examined its internal computations, identified a direction associated with repetition, and directly modified 131,072 weights, or 0.016% of the total. There was no additional gradient-descent training. Its MATH-500 score rose from 7.9% to 48.1% (<v0>Takehi et al., Sparks of Weight-Space Programming, Experiment 8</v0> (research blog, not peer reviewed; published: 2026-11-02; accessed: 2026-11-22)).
이 결과를 모델이 수학을 새로 배웠다고 읽어서는 안 된다. 같은 글의 추: This does not mean the model learned new mathematics. In an additional experiment, Astra could not improve MATH-500 performance by more than approximately one percentage point for Gemma 3 270M, a model without the repetition problem. The authors concluded that weight editing could remove obstacles hiding existing capabilities but did not add absent ones. Wang and colleagues at UC San Diego argued that the edit was a form of activation steering, an existing technique that pushes internal activations in a particular direction, and that suppressing repetition largely explained the gain (<v0>Wang et al., A closer look at “Sparks of Weight-Space Programming”</v0> (LessWrong post, not peer reviewed; published: 2026-11-17; accessed: 2026-11-22)).
해석은 아직 열려 있다. 그래도 사전학습과 사후학습이 모델을 만드는 마지: The interpretation remains open. Still, this raises the possibility that pretraining and post-training may not be the final steps in building models. Might we eventually ask AI to “find why this model keeps failing and fix it,” rather than only teaching it example answers?
이 절은 코딩 모델이 사전학습으로 기반을, 사후학습으로 쓰임새를 얻는 과: This section examined how pretraining builds a coding model’s foundation and post-training adapts it for use. Yet the resulting model still outputs text. Who writes that code to files, runs tests, and revises it after failures? Section 8.3 examines tool calls and the external program that executes them.
학술 자료는 게재처의 종류를, 그 밖의 자료는 자료의 성격을 함께 적었다: Academic sources identify the type of publication venue; other sources identify the nature of the material.

8.1절은 모델이 다음 토큰을 하나씩 예측해 코드를 써 내려가는 원리를,: Section 8.1 explains how models write code by predicting one token at a time; Section 8.2 explains how training produces those models. Both describe models that output text. Yet the coding agents in Sections 3.2 and 3.5 edit files, run tests, and revise code after failures. There is a gap between producing text and executing a program. This section explains how that gap is bridged.
The bridge lies outside the model. The model executes nothing itself. It produces formatted text requesting that a capability run with particular inputs. An external program reads the text and performs the actual execution. That program is the harness, whose overall structure is discussed in Section 7.1. Here, we focus on calling and executing tools.
이 절의 질문은 두 가지다. 1) 도구 호출은 어떤 구조로 이루어지고,: This section asks two questions: 1) How are tool calls structured, and what do coding agents use as tools? 2) Why and how is execution controlled? Section 7.3 covers selecting and connecting tools, Section 9.3 covers attacks using hidden instructions and their defenses, Section 10.3 covers tracing agent behavior through call records, and Section 17.4 covers the effects of standardized tool protocols.
Descriptions drawn from product documentation were checked on November 18, 2026. The cited product documents do not identify their own versions, so only access dates are given. Versioned materials, including the MCP specification, Transformers documentation, and public repositories, also include a version or commit. Product capabilities and defaults may change later.
도구 호출의 구조: The structure of a tool call
이 절에서 도구(tool)는 모델이 실행을 요청할 수 있도록 하네스가 이: Here, a tool is a capability the harness exposes with a name, description, and input format so the model can request its execution. File reading, shell-command execution, meaning commands entered in a terminal, and web search can each be tools. Output requesting a tool’s execution is a tool call. Anthropic calls the capability tool use; OpenAI calls it function calling or tool calling. Anthropic’s documentation also notes the term function calling (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18); <v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)).
두 문서가 설명하는 흐름도 같다. 이 절은 그 흐름을 네 단계로 정리한다: Both documents describe the same flow, summarized here in four stages (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)).
하네스가 모델에 요청을 보낼 때, 사용자의 지시와 함께 쓸 수 있는 도구: When sending a request, the harness includes the available tool list alongside the user’s instructions. Each entry is a tool definition.
모델은 도구가 필요하다고 판단하면 사용자에게 줄 답 대신 도구 호출을 출: If the model decides it needs a tool, it outputs a tool call instead of a user-facing answer. The call includes the tool name and input values.
The harness interprets the call and executes the corresponding capability.
하네스가 실행 결과를 대화 기록에 덧붙여 모델에 다시 보낸다. 이 결과를: The harness appends the execution result to conversation history and sends it back to the model. This is the tool result.
모델은 결과를 보고 다음 호출을 출력하거나, 더 부를 도구가 없으면 사용: The model uses the result to produce another call or, if no more tools are needed, an answer to the user. Repeating stages 2 through 4 forms the agentic loop. This is the loop referred to by Simon Willison’s definition cited in Section 3.2: an agent is a model that repeatedly runs tools to achieve a goal.
형식을 예시로 보면 다음과 같다. Anthropic 문서의 형식을 따라: The following examples illustrate the format. They were constructed for this section using Anthropic’s documented format; real requests and responses contain additional fields. They use JSON, JavaScript Object Notation, a text format representing data as name-value pairs. First is the tool definition the harness supplies to the model.
도구 정의는 이름, 설명, 입력 형식으로 이루어진다. 입력 형식은 JSO: A tool definition consists of a name, description, and input format. The input uses JSON Schema; the definition above requires one string named <v0/>. The description is natural language. The model uses it and the user’s request to decide whether to call the tool. A model deciding to run tests produces text such as the following.
<v0/>는 Python 코드의 테스트를 실행하는 명령이다. 이 출력은: <v0/> is a command for running Python tests. This output requests execution; nothing has run yet. After executing the command, the harness returns its output in the following form.
모델 쪽에서 보면 이 과정은 8.1절에서 본 다음 토큰 예측과 다르지 않: For the model, this remains the next-token prediction described in Section 8.1. Tool definitions become part of the prompt rather than arriving through a separate channel. Anthropic explains that the API constructs a special system prompt from tool definitions and settings and publishes its template (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)). Open-weight models make the textual nature of calls directly visible. In the Hugging Face Transformers example, Hermes-2-Pro-Llama-3-8B directly generates JSON containing the tool name and inputs between <v1/> markers. Developer code interprets the string and executes the tool (<v2/> (Transformers documentation v5.17.0; accessed: 2026-11-18)). Anthropic’s template likewise mentions interpreting model output with regular expressions. The <v3/> block above is therefore the API’s parsed representation of model-generated text.
생성된 텍스트가 형식을 지킨다는 보장은 두 곳에서 나온다. 하나는 학습이: Two mechanisms support correct output formatting. One is training, discussed below. The other is a generation-time constraint. OpenAI describes converting JSON Schema into a context-free grammar and, at each generation step, setting the probability of grammatically invalid tokens to zero. This is constrained decoding. In its internal evaluation of complex-schema adherence, gpt-4o-2024-08-06 achieved 93% through training alone and 100% with this constraint (<v0/> (published: 2024-08-06)). Anthropic likewise states that enabling <v1/> in tool definitions guarantees schema-conforming inputs through constraints based on the same principle (<v2/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)). The guarantee covers format only. OpenAI notes that values can still be wrong. In the example, <v3/> is guaranteed to be a string, not a command that is safe to execute.
Three consequences follow from this structure.
첫째, 실행을 결정하는 자리는 하네스에 있다. 모델은 도구가 어떻게 구현: First, execution decisions reside in the harness. The model sees tool definitions and returned results, not the implementation (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)). The harness decides whether to execute a generated call as written, seek human approval, or reject it. Permission rules, approvals, and sandboxes discussed below operate at this point.
둘째, 에이전트가 한 일은 호출과 결과의 기록으로 남는다. 호출과 결과가: Second, an agent’s actions leave call-and-result records, because both pass through the harness as text. For example, Claude Code documentation states that messages, tool uses, and results are individually recorded in files on the user’s computer (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)). These records let us retrace what the agent read and changed and help answer Part III’s question of how to trust its work. Section 10.3 explains how to read and use them.
셋째, 도구는 컨텍스트 윈도(context window, 모델이 한 번에: Third, tools occupy the context window, the limit on tokens a model can consult at once. Tool definitions enter each request, and calls and results accumulate in conversation history. Anthropic states that tool names, descriptions, input formats, calls, and results all count as tokens. OpenAI likewise says function definitions count toward context limits and are billed as input tokens (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18); <v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)). More tools and longer results increase costs and reduce the space available for the task.
비용은 루프의 구조 때문에 더 빨리 는다. 하네스는 호출이 한 번 끝날: The loop structure accelerates cost growth. After each call, the harness appends the new result to all messages so far and sends another request, repeatedly submitting the earlier content. Assuming similar additions per call, cumulative input tokens grow with the square of the call count. This calculation is the section author’s estimate. Prompt caching reduces the burden. Anthropic documents caching of the request prefix, ordered as tool definitions, system prompt, and messages. Cache-read tokens cost 0.1 times the base input price, with multipliers varying by model. Since tool definitions come first, changing them invalidates the entire cache (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)). Sections 5.2 and 6.3 discuss context-window management.
도구 호출 능력은 어떻게 만들어졌나: How did models learn to call tools?
모델이 위와 같은 형식의 호출을 출력하는 것은 그렇게 하도록 만들어졌기: Models produce calls in these formats because they were designed to do so. Section 3.2 covered product-release history; here, we examine where the call format was specified.
처음에는 형식이 프롬프트에 있었다. Yao 등의 ReAct는 모델에게 예: Initially, it was in the prompt. Yao and colleagues’ ReAct showed a few examples that led models to alternate reasoning and acting in text. An external program executed the written action and appended the result to the next input. The paper used a simple Wikipedia-search API, an application programming interface through which programs call other programs’ capabilities, for question answering and fact verification (<v0>Yao et al., ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models</v0> (ICLR 2023 main conference; preprint released: 2022-10-06)). This had the same loop structure described above, but format adherence depended on the prompted examples.
다음에는 형식이 학습으로 옮겨 갔다. Schick 등의 Toolforme: Next, the format moved into training. Schick and colleagues’ Toolformer taught a model which API to call, when, with which inputs, and how to use its result. API calls were represented as text inserted into ordinary prose. The authors showed an existing language model a few examples, had it propose calls within text, executed those calls, and retained only cases where including the call and result reduced subsequent token-prediction loss by a threshold amount. This selected calls useful to prediction without human answer labels. Tools included a calculator, question-answering system, search engine, translation system, and calendar (<v0>Schick et al., Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools</v0> (NeurIPS 2023 main conference; preprint released: 2023-02-09)). In June 2023, OpenAI added API functionality that takes JSON Schema function descriptions and returns JSON arguments. OpenAI said its models were fine-tuned to recognize when to call functions and produce correctly formatted JSON (<v1/> (published: 2023-06-13)). Current documentation offers a similar explanation. Anthropic says models call its predefined tools for shell execution, file editing, and desktop or browser interaction more reliably because they learned those input formats (<v2/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)). Section 8.2 covers the training that develops these capabilities.
도구를 모델에 연결하는 방식도 규약으로 정리되었다. Anthropic은: Tool connections were also standardized. In November 2024, Anthropic introduced MCP, the Model Context Protocol, citing the need to implement separate integrations for each data source (<v0/> (published: 2024-11-25)). MCP calls the capability-providing program a server and the consuming AI application a client. It specifies messages for requesting tool lists and calling tools. Returned tool definitions likewise include names, descriptions, and input formats (<v1/> (specification version: 2025-11-25; accessed: 2026-11-18)). In December 2025, Anthropic donated MCP to the Linux Foundation’s newly established Agentic AI Foundation. The Foundation’s press release reported more than 10,000 public MCP servers (<v2/> (published: 2025-12-09)). That server count is the announcing organization’s figure. Section 7.3 discusses connecting and designing MCP servers, and Section 17.4 examines standardization’s ecosystem effects.
Coding-agent harnesses expose work developers perform on computers as tools. Claude Code documentation groups built-in tools into file operations, search, execution, web, and code intelligence, including checking type errors after edits and jumping to definitions. Other capabilities are added through extensions such as MCP (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)). Products differ in tool names and grouping. This section instead groups tools by what they affect: files, commands, web and browsers, and external-service APIs. This author-defined classification supports the later discussion of controls.
파일 읽기, 내용 검색, 수정, 새 파일 만들기: Read, search, and edit files; create new files
읽기와 검색은 아무것도 바꾸지 않는다. 수정은 작업 폴더의 파일을 바꾼다: Reading and searching change nothing. Editing changes files in the working folder.
테스트, 빌드, 버전 관리, 패키지 설치 같은 셸 명령 실행: Run shell commands for tests, builds, version control, package installation, and similar tasks
사용자가 터미널에서 할 수 있는 일을 대부분 할 수 있다. 파일 삭제와: Can perform most actions available to a terminal user, including deleting files and sending data externally.
웹 검색, 문서 가져오기, 브라우저 화면 조작: Search the web, retrieve documents, and operate browser interfaces
다른 사람이 쓴 글이 모델의 입력으로 들어온다. 화면 조작은 로그인된 서: Other people’s text enters model input. Interface actions may change the state of signed-in services.
이슈 관리 도구, 데이터베이스, 배포 시스템 등의 기능 호출: Call capabilities in issue trackers, databases, deployment systems, and similar services
표의 오른쪽 열이 대상마다 다르다는 점이 뒤에서 중요해진다. 되돌릴 수: The differences in the rightmost column will matter later. Reversibility also differs. The same Claude Code documentation says file edits can be undone through checkpoints preserving earlier contents, whereas remote actions involving databases, APIs, and deployment cannot be undone by checkpoints.
명령어 도구는 넷 가운데 범위가 가장 넓다. 테스트 실행과 파일 삭제가: Command tools have the broadest scope of the four. The same tool runs tests and deletes files, so its name alone is not enough to decide whether execution should be permitted. Browser and desktop interaction can also be exposed as tools in the same format. Section 16.4 covers agents that operate interfaces.

The record illustrates the distinction. The subagent reported that it had not committed because the folder was not a git repository, yet no call ran a git command. Its only basis was the absence of a <v0/> folder in the listing from step 1, as the agent itself acknowledged while transcribing the record. An independent check confirmed the conclusion. Still, not every statement in the report had been verified by execution. Call results provide the evidence for judging completion. This is the distinction Section 3.5 makes between a completion claim and evidence of completion.
하네스가 보고한 사용량은 도구 호출 6회, 실행 시간 약 13.6초, 토: The harness reported six tool calls, approximately 13.6 seconds, and 68,999 tokens to change one line. The environment does not break down token usage, so its components are unknown. The total is nevertheless consistent with the earlier explanation that each request resubmits tool definitions and accumulated history.
모델이 보는 것은 도구 정의와 도구 결과의 텍스트다. 그러므로 같은 모델: The model sees the text of tool definitions and results. Even the same model may therefore produce different outcomes depending on how that text is constructed.
Yang 등은 이 차이를 직접 비교했다. 저자들은 에이전트가 컴퓨터를 다: Yang and colleagues directly tested this difference. They called the interface through which agents operate a computer the agent-computer interface (ACI), redesigning file viewing, searching, and editing commands for models. On SWE-bench Lite, a 300-problem subset of a benchmark using real open-source repository issues, an agent given only a shell solved 11.00%, while an agent using the same GPT-4 Turbo model with the new interface solved 18.00% (<v0>Yang et al., SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering</v0> (NeurIPS 2024 main conference; Table 1)). In component comparisons, showing files in 100-line windows scored 18.0%, versus 12.7% for whole files. An edit command rejecting syntax-breaking changes scored 18.0%, versus 15.0% without that check (Table 3). These results concern a 2024 model and a specific benchmark, not current performance. The transferable lesson is that an interface convenient for people need not suit a model, and more information is not always better. Section 3.2 discusses changes in SWE-bench scores; Section 10.4 explains how to interpret benchmarks.
호출을 어떤 형식으로 적게 하느냐도 비교되었다. Wang 등의 CodeA: Call formats have also been compared. Wang and colleagues’ CodeAct made models express actions as executable Python rather than JSON or a fixed text format. Code can connect several tool calls within one output. Across 17 models, the authors reported success rates up to 20% higher (<v0>Wang et al., Executable Code Actions Elicit Better LLM Agents</v0> (ICML 2024 main conference)), using API-Bank and a new benchmark they created.
Anthropic의 엔지니어링 블로그는 같은 생각을 MCP에 적용한 사례: An Anthropic engineering post applied this idea to MCP. Direct tool calls pass all definitions and intermediate results through the context window. If the model instead writes tool-calling code executed in a separate environment, it can read only necessary definitions and process intermediate results there. In one example, reported token usage fell from 150,000 to 2,000, a 98.7% reduction (<v0/> (published: 2025-11-04)). This is one company-blog example without detailed measurement conditions, not a general savings rate. The post also identifies a cost: executing model-written code requires a separate environment with sandboxing, resource limits, and monitoring.
도구를 만드는 쪽의 지침도 같은 방향을 가리킨다. Anthropic의 다: Guidance for tool developers points in the same direction. Another Anthropic post describes tools as “a contract between deterministic systems and non-deterministic agents.” It recommends a small set of clearly purposed tools, concise results, and error messages explaining what to fix (<v0/> (published: 2025-09-11)). This, too, is a company engineering blog summarizing its own experience. Returning an execution failure as a result is part of interface design. The MCP specification recommends reporting execution errors, such as invalid inputs, in tool results so the model can correct its arguments and retry (<v1/> (specification version: 2025-11-25; accessed: 2026-11-18)). Section 7.3 covers tool selection and descriptions.
틀린 출력이 실행으로 이어질 때: When incorrect output becomes an executed action
도구가 없는 모델의 오류는 화면에 나타난 문장으로 남고, 그 문장을 쓸지: For a model without tools, an error remains text on a screen, and a person decides whether to use it. A tool-using agent can express the same error as a call that executes unless the harness blocks it. There are two broad routes from output to execution.
하나는 잘못된 호출이다. 없는 파일을 열거나, 입력값을 틀리게 넣거나,: One is an incorrect call: opening a nonexistent file, supplying wrong inputs, or selecting an unsuitable tool. Patil and colleagues’ Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL) specifically evaluates call accuracy. They reported that recent models handle single calls well but still struggle with the memory, contextual judgment, and extended reasoning needed for multistep tasks (<v0>Patil et al., The Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL): From Tool Use to Agentic Evaluation of Large Language Models</v0> (ICML 2025 main conference)). Malformed calls usually return errors and can be retried. Correctly formatted calls with incorrect content are harder: a command deleting a folder that must be preserved can execute without error.
다른 하나는 오염된 입력이다. 도구 결과는 모델의 입력이 되므로, 도구가: The other route is contaminated input. Tool results enter model input, so an agent may follow instruction-like text in a retrieved page or document. Greshake and colleagues called this indirect prompt injection and demonstrated in real services and experimental applications that retrieved text can alter application behavior, including whether and how it calls other APIs (<v0>Greshake et al., Not What You’ve Signed Up For: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection</v0> (AISec ’23, ACM CCS workshop paper)). The problem is structural: model input does not reliably separate instructions from data. System prompts, user requests, and tool results form one token sequence, and the model cannot reliably assign authority according to a sentence’s origin (<v1/> (personal blog; published: 2025-06-16)). When introducing function calling in 2023, OpenAI likewise warned that untrusted tool-output data could induce unintended actions and recommended user confirmation before consequential actions (<v2/> (published: 2023-06-13)). Instructions may hide in tool definitions as well as results. Invariant Labs demonstrated instructions hidden in an addition tool’s description causing an agent to read an SSH private key, a secret file used to authenticate access to remote servers, and pass it as a tool argument (<v3/> (published: 2025-04-01)). This source is a security-company blog, not peer reviewed. Section 9.3 covers attack types and defenses.
두 경로에서 나온 호출이 얼마나 큰 문제가 되는지는 그 행동을 되돌릴 수: The seriousness of calls arising through either route depends on reversibility. File edits have restoration mechanisms, but a harness cannot undo changes pushed to a remote repository, sent messages, deployments, or database modifications.
실행을 통제하는 세 장치: 권한 규칙, 승인, 샌드박스: Three controls on execution: permission rules, approval, and sandboxes
두 경로 모두 모델이 출력한 호출에서 시작하고, 호출은 하네스를 거쳐야: Both routes start with model-generated calls, which must pass through the harness to execute. Controls therefore belong in the harness. Training and instructions against incorrect calls also matter, but probabilistic, input-dependent model output cannot be the only barrier to execution. The following three controls are described using official Claude Code and OpenAI Codex documentation. Permission-rule examples come from Claude Code; approvals and sandboxes focus on structures common to both products.
권한 규칙은 어떤 호출을 허용하고, 어떤 호출을 사람에게 묻고, 어떤 호: Permission rules specify in advance which calls to allow, which require asking a person, and which to reject. Claude Code rules match tool names and target patterns. For example, <v0/> applies to shell commands beginning with <v1/>, and <v2/> applies to reads below a particular folder (<v3/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)). Deny rules apply in every permission mode (<v4/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)).
규칙의 한계는 모델이 쓴 명령의 글자에 적용된다는 데 있다. Claude: A limitation is that these rules match the text of model-written commands. Claude Code splits commands joined by shell operators such as <v0/> and checks each part. But alternative ways of invoking the same program can evade a rule. Its documentation therefore says Bash rules are not a security boundary around a program. For example, denying <v1/> does not match an invocation written as <v2/>. It recommends sandboxing when restrictions must not depend on command spelling (<v3/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)).
승인은 호출을 실행하기 전에 사람에게 보여 주고 허락을 받는 절차다. 얼: Approval means showing a call to a person and obtaining permission before execution. Permission modes determine how often to ask. According to Claude Code documentation, Manual mode permits reads without asking but requests approval before file edits and shell commands. Auto mode uses a separate classifier model to review and block calls it judges risky; the documentation says this reduces approval requests without guaranteeing safety. Another mode skips all checks; the documentation warns that it should be used only in isolated environments such as containers or virtual machines without internet access (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)).
승인에는 한계가 있다. 요청이 잦으면 사람은 내용을 읽지 않고 허용하게: Approval has limits. Frequent requests encourage people to approve without reading. Anthropic reported that users approved approximately 93% of requests in its telemetry and explained that attention to each request decreases as their number grows (<v0/> (published: 2026-05-25)). This is approval fatigue. Approval works as a control only when a person reads and judges the request, an assumption weakened by increasing frequency. Section 6.4 discusses where to place approval points.
샌드박스(sandbox)는 프로그램이 접근할 수 있는 범위를 운영체제 수: A sandbox restricts a program’s access at the operating-system level. Permission rules and approval decide whether a command may start; the sandbox determines what it can reach while running. The restrictions cover files and networks. Claude Code’s sandbox is off by default. When enabled, shell commands and their child processes can write only to working and temporary folders, and network connections can reach only allowed domains. Operating-system mechanisms such as macOS Seatbelt and Linux bubblewrap enforce these restrictions (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)). OpenAI Codex documentation describes the same separation as two layers: the sandbox determines what the agent can technically do, and the approval policy determines when to ask a person. Local defaults disable network access and limit writes to the working folder (<v1/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)).
The implementation explains why enforcement does not depend on model judgment. Documentation for sandbox-runtime, the open runtime used by Claude Code, describes wrapping Linux processes with bubblewrap and removing their network namespace, the network environment visible to them. A sandboxed process has no direct route out; it can use only a proxy across a connected Unix domain socket, a channel between processes on the same computer. This host-side proxy checks the allowlist. On macOS, a Seatbelt profile permits communication only with a particular local port, where the proxy listens. Restrictions apply to every descendant process (<v0/> (public repository; accessed: 2026-11-18; commit 0bbebed, 2026-11-12)). They hold regardless of the command the model writes or which programs execute it.
파일 시스템과 네트워크를 함께 막아야 하는 이유는 한쪽만 막으면 다른 쪽: File and network restrictions must work together because either unrestricted side can provide a bypass. Anthropic explains that without network restrictions a compromised agent can send sensitive files such as SSH keys externally, while without file restrictions it can escape the sandbox and obtain network access (<v0/> (published: 2025-10-20)). Sandboxing also reduces approval fatigue: actions within the boundary can execute without asking because their damage remains contained. The same post reported an 84% reduction in approval requests during internal use, a company-internal result without external verification.
어떤 도구와 대상을 허용, 확인, 거부할지: Which tools and targets to allow, confirm, or reject
명령의 글자를 보고 판단하므로 같은 일을 다른 형태로 하는 호출을 놓칠: Text matching may miss differently written calls performing the same action
이 호출을 지금 실행할지: Whether to execute this call now
호출을 실행하기 전, 사람이나 분류기가 판단: Before execution, judged by a person or classifier
요청이 잦으면 읽지 않고 허용하게 된다: Frequent requests can lead to approval without reading
실행된 명령이 닿을 수 있는 파일과 네트워크의 범위: The files and networks an executing command can reach
명령이 실행되는 동안, 운영체제가 강제: Enforced by the operating system during execution
샌드박스가 감싸지 않는 도구에는 적용되지 않는다: Does not apply to tools outside the sandbox
세 장치는 서로를 대신하지 못한다. Claude Code의 샌드박스는 셸: These controls do not replace one another. Claude Code’s sandbox covers shell commands only. File-reading, editing, and web tools operate outside it under permission rules, as do local MCP servers. Even with sandboxing enabled, reads are broadly permitted across the computer by default, so it does not prevent credential-file reading itself (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)). Network allowlists also have gaps. Anthropic described files being uploaded from a workspace to an attacker’s account through an allowed domain, concluding that allowlisting a domain effectively opens all its available capabilities rather than merely filtering destinations (<v1/> (published: 2026-05-25)). The MCP specification likewise recommends keeping a person able to reject calls in the loop, showing users tool arguments, and recording tool use for trust and security (<v2/> (specification version: 2025-11-25; accessed: 2026-11-18)).
격리의 강도에도 단계가 있다. Claude Code의 문서는 명령 단위의: Isolation also has levels. Claude Code documentation compares command-level sandboxes, a sandbox runtime around the entire harness process, containers, and virtual machines. Virtual machines, with their own kernel, the operating system’s core, provide the strongest separation. The same document warns that isolation reduces the impact of compromise without eliminating risk: accessible data can still leak through any open outbound network route (<v0/> (accessed: 2026-11-18)).
어느 단계를 고를지는 사용자가 누구인지에 따라 달라진다. 승인은 사용자가: The appropriate level depends on the user. Approval provides control only when the user can judge the request. Anthropic’s previously cited How we contain Claude across products explains tailoring isolation to users’ ability to supervise agents. Claude Code, mainly used by developers able to read shell commands, uses approvals and operating-system sandboxing. Claude Cowork, used by many people unfamiliar with shell commands, uses a local virtual machine rather than relying on approval. The same reasoning applies to people who work by checking results without reading code: boundaries enforced without their judgment are preferable to asking about every command. These last two sentences are this section author’s interpretation.
이 구조에서, 에이전트에게 작업을 맡기기 전에 확인할 것을 세 가지로 정: This structure suggests three checks before delegating a task. These are the author’s recommendations from the material above, not a research-validated procedure.
이 작업에서 에이전트가 할 수 있는 행동 가운데 되돌릴 수 없는 것은 무: Which available actions cannot be undone? If pushing to remote repositories, deploying, modifying databases, or sending messages is possible, retain approval for those calls rather than allowing them automatically.
에이전트가 읽게 될 것 가운데 내가 쓰지 않은 텍스트는 무엇인가. 웹페이: Which texts the agent will read were written by someone else? If web pages, external documents, or third-party MCP descriptions enter the session, do not simultaneously expose secret-bearing files and network access.
묻지 않고 실행되게 한 범위가 운영체제 수준의 경계 안에 있는가. 승인을: Is approval-free execution confined within an operating-system boundary? Before skipping approvals, establish a sandbox or container boundary enforced independently of model judgment.
두 번째 항목은 앞에서 인용한 Willison의 글이 치명적 삼중 조합(: The second check avoids the conditions Willison’s cited article calls the lethal trifecta: combining private-data access, exposure to untrusted content, and external communication in one agent can let a hidden instruction cause data exfiltration.
이 절의 설명은 Anthropic과 OpenAI가 공개한 문서와 MCP: This section generalizes structures shared by Anthropic and OpenAI documentation and the MCP specification. Other harnesses may have different tool names, permission modes, and sandbox coverage. Product documentation was checked on November 18, 2026; defaults and mode names may change afterward. Check current defaults in the documentation for the tool actually used.
인용한 수치는 성격이 다르다. SWE-agent와 CodeAct의 수치는: The cited figures have different evidential status. SWE-agent and CodeAct results come from peer-reviewed papers but concern 2024 models and specific benchmarks. Schema adherence of 100%, approval of 93% of requests, an 84% reduction in approval requests, 98.7% token savings, and 10,000 MCP servers are company- or foundation-reported figures without independent verification. They are used only as evidence that these phenomena were reported, not to generalize effect sizes.
앞의 여섯 단계 기록은 한 번의 실행에서 얻은 것이다. 과제는 작은 연습: The six-step record comes from one run on a one-line bug in a small practice project. The table is the agent’s transcription, not an original harness log; only call count and test output were checked independently. It illustrates how calls and results connect, not how well agents fix bugs. It cannot establish call counts or failure rates on larger tasks, and rerunning the same task may change both call order and count.
세 장치를 모두 갖추어도 남는 문제가 있다. 형식과 권한은 맞지만 의도와: Problems remain even with all three controls. A correctly formatted, permitted call that conflicts with intent, such as editing the wrong file within an allowed working folder, triggers none of them. Review and tests after execution must catch such changes. Section 9.2 discusses unrequested edits, and Chapter 10 discusses checking results with tests.
기록이 남는다는 것과 사람이 그 기록을 읽는다는 것도 별개다. 호출이 수: Having records and having people read them are also different matters. After dozens of calls, reading everything becomes difficult. Section 10.3 discusses what to retain verbatim and what to summarize.
모델은 텍스트를 출력하고, 하네스가 그 가운데 도구 호출을 골라 실행한: The model outputs text; the harness identifies tool calls, executes them, and returns results as text. Repeating this process lets agents edit files and run tests. Because execution passes through the harness, actions can be recorded and controlled there with permission rules, approvals, and sandboxes. The information shown and returned to the model, and its format, change the outcome. Model and harness therefore jointly determine agent performance and safety.
이 루프가 코드 작업에서 돌아가려면 조건이 하나 더 필요하다. 도구 결과: One further condition is needed for this loop to work on code. Tool results must return quickly and clearly to inform the next decision. Execution and tests serve this role in coding. Section 8.4 examines this property.
